tagline.text: A hike to Cebu City's highest ridge at 752 m, with views over the city

location.label: Location
location.text: Babag mountain range northwest of Cebu City; the village of Napo above Guadalupe is the main jump-off

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (per person, transport, meals and snacks; guide or tour extra)

children.text: Mount Babag is a mountain of about 752 meters above sea level, known as the highest point in Cebu City. The classic day hike goes up from Guadalupe to the village of Napo, past rivers, waterfalls and mango groves, to a ridge with views of Cebu City.

Mount Babag lies in the Babag mountain range northwest of Cebu City, and its elevation of about 752 meters above sea level is known as the highest point in the city. The Babag range is a long ridge about 25 kilometers from north to south and about 4 kilometers across at its widest, and the name "Babag" is explained as a Cebuano word meaning "to obstruct." Communication relay towers stand near the summit and are now enclosed by a protective barrier, and the Boy Scouts are said to have once camped here.

The most common way to hike is to take a jeepney from downtown Cebu City to Guadalupe Church, ride a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) up to the village of Napo, and start walking there. The Napo basketball court is the usual starting point, and the trail follows the Sapangdaku River to the Lower Kahugan Spring, where it splits in two. One branch is the wide, gentle Kahugan Trail, and the other is the shorter Busan Trail, a degree or two harder. Ernie's Trail, which branches off the Busan Trail, is the steepest and most direct route, with inclines of 65 to 70 degrees where you climb using handholds. Walking times depend on the route and your fitness. A mountaineering guide site lists about 4–5 hours to the summit and rates it a "minor climb" at difficulty 4 out of 9, while another account says 2.5 to 4 hours depending on the route. Day hikers are advised to start early in the morning, and those camping to go up in mid-afternoon. There are also other routes, such as the Manggapares Trail, where the incline is nonstop all the way to the ridge, so check route names and steepness in advance. Waterfalls, city views and open trails are listed as the features of this mountain.

The whole mountain feels like mango country. Mango, santol, jackfruit, duhat, tamarind, avocado, star apple, coconut, bamboo and madre de cacao grow throughout, and in the rainy season people are said to catch catfish, freshwater crabs and rare shrimp in the river. Birds are recorded too, including kingfishers, the Brahminy kite and the rare endemic black shama. The ridge trail was long used as a lookout and a base of Cebuano resistance against the Spanish, Americans and Japanese, and it is described as the site of the last fighting during the liberation of Cebu, when American troops and Cebuano guerrillas fought the Japanese.

This guide is for travelers staying in Cebu City who want a half-day or full-day hike. It draws on 2011–2012 pieces from a mountaineering site together with more recent guides, so fees and trail conditions may have changed. Guide companies and clubs change their schedules often, so contact them before you go, and if it is your first time it is safer to go with a Cebu mountaineering club or an experienced hiker.

From Guadalupe, follow the concrete and asphalt road past the village of Sapangdaku to reach Napo. The Napo basketball court is the usual starting point, and parking is said to be available. You can walk up, but most people ride a motorcycle to save energy. The Napo trail climbs along the Sapangdaku River and includes a river crossing. The Lower Kahugan Spring is both a place to refill water and rest and the point where the trails split, so decide there which way to go. After heavy rain the river can rise and become dangerous.

The Kahugan Trail is long, wide and easy, and it is the main route residents use to carry produce down to Guadalupe. The Busan Trail is shorter but a bit harder, so pick one to match your fitness. On both you can refill water and rest at springs or farmhouses.

You meet these falls higher up the Kahugan Trail, and one description presents them as four waterfalls. They are often used as the first rest stop in a day itinerary. In the rainy season the water rises and crossing is dangerous, so watch the weather.
A steep trail branching right off the Busan Trail, it drops into a small hanging valley, crosses a brook, and then climbs 65–70 degree slopes using handholds. It takes about
55–90 minutes
from the Roble homestead to the ridge and is also used as a training ground by outdoor clubs. It is not recommended for beginners.
A rest stop on the Busan Trail, where the family sells green coconuts cheaply and mobile signal is good. Itineraries often have hikers eat lunch here and then continue up to the ridge.

From the ridge you can look down on Cebu City and the surrounding mountains. Following Babag Ridge Road northeast takes you to Upper Busay, and going down Veteran's Drive brings you out near JY Square in Lahug.

The hill above the former Swiss Chalet restaurant site is the main campsite, holding 20–35 tents and easy to reach from Veteran's Drive in Busay via the ridge road. Manwel's Peak (One-Bamboo Hill), about 150 meters from the summit, is a quiet spot for up to nine tents with a 360-degree view and is described as the safest campsite.

Kingfishers, the Brahminy kite and the rare black shama have been recorded here, and mango, jackfruit, avocado and bamboo line the trail. If you have binoculars, an early-morning hike is even more enjoyable.

items.title: Day hike
items.subtitle: From Napo via the Roble homestead and the ridge, down to Kalunasan

children.text: Meet at the Guadalupe parking lot, buy breakfast and snacks, and get ready to head to Napo. One guide notes that you can buy ingredients for a packed lunch at the small market behind the church.
Start walking at Napo and follow the Sapangdaku River to the Lower Kahugan Spring, where you refill water.
Climb to the Busay Lut-od Waterfalls and rest.
Rest at the Roble homestead with a green coconut and prepare lunch.
Climb to Babag Ridge via the East Ridge Pass.
After looking down on the city from the ridge, descend to Kalunasan by the No-Santol Tree Trail and return to Guadalupe.
These times are an example based on the schedule in an older guide. Actual times depend on your pace and rest stops, so leave plenty of margin to get down before dark.

items.title: Ridge traverse
items.subtitle: Climb from Napo and descend toward Busay

children.text: Take a jeepney from downtown Cebu City to Guadalupe, then a motorcycle up to Napo.
Climb to the ridge by the Kahugan Trail or the Busan Trail.
Eat lunch and rest on the ridge. If you plan to camp in the afternoon, move to Manwel's Peak or the old Swiss Chalet site.
Walk down Babag Ridge Road northeast to Upper Busay.
Go down Veteran's Drive to JY Square in Lahug and return to your hotel by taxi or Grab.
There are many direct flights a day from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB), and the flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Airlines and timetables change by season, so check when you book.
Use a taxi or Grab from the airport to downtown Cebu City, and travel to the mountain separately from downtown.
By public transport, take a jeepney bound for Guadalupe Church from downtown and get off at Guadalupe. An older guide gave the round trip between downtown and Guadalupe as
, so it has probably risen since.
By car, take Escario Street or Gorordo Avenue to Guadalupe, continue past Sapangdaku up to Napo, where you can park.
In the older guide, a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) from Guadalupe to Napo cost
for one person, or
each when two rode together. A 2025 blog put it at about ₱30–50, but it is now a negotiated price, so agree on it first.
A paved road also climbs slowly past the village of Sapangdaku and can be walked.
From the ridge toward Busay you can come out at JY Square in Lahug along Veteran's Drive.
There is also a way down to the Kalunasan Circumferential Road below, which the older guide said is cheaper and shorter.

The best time to hike is the dry season from December to May, and you should start early in the morning to avoid the midday heat. If you camp, one guide advises going up in late afternoon to see sunset and sunrise.
Avoid the trail during or right after rain, when it is very slippery. Streams and waterfalls can also swell.

There is almost no traveler accommodation near the mountain, so most people stay in downtown Cebu City and hike as a day trip. If you camp, use the old Swiss Chalet site or Manwel's Peak, and confirm lodging and camping rules locally. Hotel names and rates change by season, so check recent reviews on a booking site.

Before the hike you can buy rice, side dishes and ingredients at the small market behind Guadalupe Church, and the church's south gate sells cheap fruit and vegetables. One guide says green coconuts are sold cheaply at the Roble homestead. After the hike, downtown Cebu City is a good place to eat Cebuano food such as grilled meat, lechon and puso.
You can refill water at the Lower Kahugan Spring, Upper Kahugan and the Roble homestead, so carry plenty.
Start early in the morning to avoid the midday sun and afternoon showers.
Ernie's Trail has many sections where you pull yourself up by hand, so beginners should choose the Kahugan Trail.
Shop in Guadalupe before you start, because you can hardly buy anything on the mountain.
Guide companies and clubs change their schedules, so contact them in advance to confirm.
Mobile signal is said to be good at the Roble homestead but varies by section, so download your map beforehand.
Decide your descent (Busay or Kalunasan) in advance and get down before dark.
With binoculars you can enjoy spotting birds such as kingfishers and kites.
The Napo trail includes a river crossing, so bring shoes that can get wet and spare socks.
The trail is very slippery on rainy days and right after rain, and streams rise. Postpone the hike if the weather is bad.
Ernie's Trail requires climbing 65–70 degree slopes by hand, so it needs fitness and gear.
There are no shops on the mountain, so bring your own water and food.
Some trails are unmarked, so go with an experienced person to avoid getting lost.
The fares and transport information here partly rely on 2011–2012 articles, so confirm them again locally.

Do not enter the fenced area around the communication towers near the summit. In July 2025 Cebu City filed a draft ordinance requiring registration with the barangay for outdoor activities in mountain barangays (Babag is not named), so check with the barangay before you go.
After the hike you can visit the Santo Niño Basilica, Magellan's Cross and more in downtown
Cebu City
If you descend toward Busay, nearby
Tops Lookout
is a good place to finish with a view of the city.
This flower garden on the same Busay highlands,
Sirao Flower Garden
, can be added to your day.
Cebu IT Park
is a lively district that is convenient for a meal and a rest after the hike.
